messages.text: Inside the Solheim Cup: How players embraced 'insane' first-tee experience

metadata.summary: Team Europe captain Anna Nordqvist said that the Solheim Cup first tee would be 'the place to be in the golfing world,' with that pre-tournament assessment spot on as she witnessed a spectacle unlike any other in the women's game.
metadata.content: Solheim Cup: How Team Europe and Team USA stars embraced first-tee party and 'insane' atmosphere at Bernardus Golf | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to content Solheim Cup: How Team Europe and Team USA stars embraced first-tee party and 'insane' atmosphere at Bernardus Golf What was the first-tee atmosphere like at the Solheim Cup? How a party atmosphere at Bernardus Golf brought an entertaining start to Team Europe's bid to regain the trophy in the Netherlands; watch the Solheim Cup live on Sky Sports Golf By Ali Stafford at Bernardus Golf Friday 11 September 2026 14:39, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Megan Khang tee off in style at this year's Solheim Cup, after she hyped up the crowd to encourage more noise Team Europe captain Anna Nordqvist said that the Solheim Cup first tee would be 'the place to be in the golfing world,' with that pre-tournament assessment spot on as she witnessed a spectacle unlike any other in the women's game. The horseshoe-shaped grandstand around the first tee at Bernardus Golf was close to capacity long before daylight, with nearly 3,000 spectators - and plenty more along the fairway - creating a party-like atmosphere of noise and excitement. United States captain Angela Stanford danced onto the tee after emerging from the tunnel, a walk Charley Hull said earlier in the week was like 'entering an arena', with vice-captains - from both sides - doing their best to make things even louder. messages.text: Sky Sports agrees three-year US Open extension

metadata.summary: Sky has agreed a three-year extension to its US Open deal, ensuring Sky Sports and NOW remains the exclusive home of the tournament in the UK and Ireland until the end of 2030.
metadata.content: US Open: Sky Sports agrees three-year extension to show the US Open until end of 2030 | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to content US Open: Sky Sports agrees three-year extension to show the US Open until end of 2030 Sky Sports agrees three-year extension to broadcast the US Open; 2026 competition reaches thrilling conclusion at Flushing Meadows this weekend; watch Aryna Sabalenka take on Elena Rybakina in the women's final on Saturday, followed by the men's final on Sunday Friday 11 September 2026 14:26, UK Image: Sky has agreed a three-year extension to its US Open deal Sky has agreed a three-year extension to its US Open deal, ensuring Sky Sports and NOW remains the exclusive home of the tournament in the UK and Ireland until the end of 2030. As part of the partnership with the United States Tennis Association (USTA), Sky Sports will retain exclusive live coverage of all men's and women's singles, doubles, mixed doubles, juniors and wheelchair competitions throughout the three-week tournament. The agreement was negotiated by the USTA's media rights partner, IMG. Alongside broadcast rights, fans in the UK and Ireland will also be able to catch up on all the action with clips and highlights available across Sky's digital and social platforms. This year's coverage has featured augmented reality graphics, enhanced data integrations, in-depth touchscreen analysis and behind-the-scenes content, bringing fans closer to the action than ever before. messages.text: Korda, Corpuz thrash Hull, Woad to make history in tied foursomes session

metadata.summary: Nelly Korda and Allisen Corpuz created Solheim Cup history with their statement victory over Charley Hull and Lottie Woad in the Friday foursomes, as Team Europe and Team USA shared the spoils in the opening session.
metadata.content: Solheim Cup 2026: Nelly Korda, Allisen Corpuz thrash Charley Hull, Lottie Woad to make history for Team USA in Friday foursomes | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to content Solheim Cup 2026: Nelly Korda, Allisen Corpuz thrash Charley Hull, Lottie Woad to make history for Team USA in Friday foursomes Team Europe and Team USA both won two points during the opening session of the Solheim Cup in the Netherlands; Nelly Korda and Allisen Corpuz extended their 100 per cent record together in foursomes; watch live on Sky Sports Golf By Ali Stafford at Bernardus Golf Friday 11 September 2026 14:38, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Friday foursomes from the Solheim Cup at Bernardus Golf, in the Netherlands Nelly Korda and Allisen Corpuz created Solheim Cup history with their statement victory over Charley Hull and Lottie Woad in the Friday foursomes, as Team Europe and Team USA shared the spoils in the opening session. Hull had won two of her previous three Solheim Cup matches against Korda, including a dominant 6&4 singles victory two years ago, although saw her and Woad dominated by the American pair in the opening match at Bernardus Golf. Korda and Corpuz recovered from losing the first hole to race to a 4&3 victory, seeing them become the first American pair in Solheim Cup history to win five foursomes matches together and the first - from either side - to win five matches in a row.
